contract.lifetime: One DownloadsPage manager per application data directory, attached once to each BrowserWidget. Hiding the page leaves transfers running. Manager teardown cancels its owned transfers and records unfinished work as interrupted.
contract.selection: Default native save-file dialog obtains an explicit destination and overwrite confirmation. A destination-chooser seam lets the controlled tests select only temporary fixture paths.
contract.history: Atomic downloads.json with version1,500-entry maximum,4MiB file bound, strict record validation, and optimistic stale-write detection. Corrupt/externally changed history is preserved instead of overwritten.
contract.no_automatic_deletion: Downloaded files are never deleted. History entries are removed only by explicit history actions. The500-entry bound refuses new transfers with a clear-history notice rather than automatically evicting old history.
contract.clearing: clearHistory preserves all live operations, including paused/resumable interrupted transfers. History-only removal rolls back in-memory changes if persistence fails.
contract.restart: Completed records restore normally; unfinished records restore as Interrupted with resume unavailable. A closed browser's native operation cannot be reconstructed from persisted metadata.

verification.fixture: Actual WebView2 downloads from a loopback HTTP server; native destination chooser replaced with explicit temporary paths only in tests. QDesktopServices file URLs intercepted without opening files or launching applications.

upstream_audit.observed: Pinned upstream defines download results/control metadata (filename,URL,targetPath,bytes,state,active/paused/resumable flags) and Chromium-history download-table clearing. This native page implements those user-facing lifecycle concepts with its own WebView2 state adapter and JSON persistence. No dedicated transfer-handler or download-page implementation was found in the pinned source search, so exact UI parity is not asserted.
